# /verify - prove the task works, then open the PR

## When to run
- **Before opening a PR** - this is the gate; the PR carries the proof it produces.
- **On explicit request** - "verify this", "does this actually work", "prove it".

You are the **orchestrator + fixer**. Agentic verification of the task goes to a
fresh **verifier sub-agent**; the objective regression sweep is **yours**.

## Repo specifics
- **Stack** - `make build` (Go, tags `gms_pure_go`; produces `./bd`). Build trap:
  a bare `CGO_ENABLED=1 go build ./cmd/bd` fails on ICU headers - always use the
  Makefile target. Run `make doctor-build` to diagnose a broken build env.
- **Where the app runs** - n/a (pure CLI). Exercise `./bd` in a scratch dir:
  `BD=$(mktemp -d) && cd $BD && /path/to/bd init`
- **Run mode** - **local** (no dev server, no sandbox; nothing to bring up beyond
  the build)
- **Driver** - the built `./bd` binary itself (plus `git` and `dolt` when the
  task touches sync/embedded storage)
- **Auth** - n/a (local CLI; do not touch remote Dolt or Gmail creds)
- **Evidence** - write all proof to `evidence/` (gitignored)
- **Proof upload target** - `gh release upload pr-evidence evidence/... -R <owner>/beads --clobber`
  (prerelease), or paste the command output directly into the PR body

## 0. Preconditions
On a branch, not the default branch; changes committed.

## 1. Build the stack
`make build` - you own the binary; the verifier reuses it.

## 2. Verify the TASK (delegate) -> fix -> re-verify (loop)
Spawn a read-only verifier:

```
You are a read-only verifier. Do NOT edit code. Independently confirm THIS task
works by driving the built ./bd CLI. It likely has no automated spec - verify
it agentically.

TASK (what a user should now be able to do, and the observable success state):
  <intent / acceptance criteria>
HOW TO EXERCISE IT:
  make build, then run ./bd in a scratch dir (mktemp -d; ./bd init) exactly as
  an end user would: bd create / bd list / bd show / bd update / bd ready /
  bd close, plus whatever subcommands the task touches. Inspect the output
  text, exit codes, and the .beads/ state it leaves behind.
DRIVER:
  the ./bd binary built at the repo root; no browser, no server
AUTH:
  n/a

Walk the exact steps, capture the success state to evidence/ (command +
stdout/stderr + exit code; screenshots are not applicable), and judge
observed vs expected. Return ONLY:

TASK: works | broken
  expected: <criteria>
  observed: <what actually happened>
  evidence: <paths under evidence/>
```

- **broken** -> fix the implementation, then spawn a **fresh** verifier. You never
  declare the task works yourself.
- Cap at ~3 rounds; if still broken, escalate to the human with the verdict.

## 3. Regression sweep - you run the codified checks; fix red directly
`make build && make ci-pr-lint && make test` (see `engdocs/TESTING.md`; use the
canonical commands, never improvised raw `go test`). Docs-only changes may use
the smaller docs-only checks from TESTING.md instead of the full suite. Triage
failures (real-bug vs stale-test); never weaken an assertion to go green. If a
fix here changes task behavior, re-verify (step 2).

## 4. Open the PR - lead with the proof, embed the evidence
The PR body MUST show the evidence, not just mention it: paste the verifier's
exercise transcript (command + tail of output) under a "Task verified" section,
and upload any artifacts from `evidence/` to the pr-evidence prerelease with
`gh release upload`, linking the stable URL.

## Rules
- **The task is the verdict** - a green suite with an unverified task isn't done.
- **"Does it actually work" -> an independent verifier; objective checks -> you.**
- Never open a PR until the task is verified. **Proof, not claims.** Branch -> PR only.
